facts.raw_span: progressive unilateral skin hardening on his right thigh and buttock for 7 years
motion of his right limb joint was slightly limited
ill-defined, stony-hard plaque involving his right thigh above the patella extending to his right buttocks with loss of skin elasticity
mild hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation
Normal results for routine blood tests
Normal results for autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Demonstrated slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Normal epidermis and mild pigmentation along the basal layer with subtle increase in density of fibroblasts extending to the subcutis and forming adipocyte entrapment but no evidence of inflammation
Dense reticular dermis extended below well-preserved appendages
Increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis
Negative Alcian blue staining

concepts.why: The patient presents with progressive unilateral skin hardening, which is a characteristic feature of scleroderma, and the histopathological findings of dense reticular dermis and increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and subcutaneous tissue thickening, along with the histopathological findings of adipocyte entrapment, are consistent with lipodermatosclerosis.
The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and hypertrichosis, along with the histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts, are consistent with fibroblastic rheumatism.
The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and subcutaneous tissue thickening, along with the histopathological findings of dense reticular dermis, are consistent with nephrogenic systemic fibrosis.
The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and the histopathological findings of normal epidermis and mild pigmentation along the basal layer are consistent with scleredema.
The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and hypertrichosis, along with the histopathological findings of adipocyte entrapment, are consistent with panniculitis.
The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and subcutaneous tissue thickening, along with the histopathological findings of dense reticular dermis, are consistent with dermatofibrosis.
The patient's symptoms of skin hardening and hypertrichosis, along with the histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts, are consistent with fibromatosis.
